author: Lauren Drapeau
title: Conn. tech schools under investigation by U.S. Dept. of Education for suspected failure to protect students - NewsBreak
text:
By Lauren Drapeau ,
7 hours ago
HARTFORD, Conn. (WTNH) — The U.S. Department of Education released a warning to the Connecticut Technical Education and Career System on Friday, claiming that it responded inaccurately to assault allegations against school staff.
The statewide school system is one of 20 districts under investigation nationwide, suspected of “passing the trash,” or allowing teachers and other school employees accused of sexual misconduct to transfer to other schools, U.S. Secretary of Education Linda McMahon said.
The school administrators have been put on notice through a “Dear Colleague” letter, restating the legal obligations that they are under to combat sexual misconduct.
Old Saybrook literacy rates: Board of Education to consider curriculum changes as parents raise concerns Connecticut Technical Education and Career System stated on Wednesday that it remains fully committed to complying with all Elementary and Secondary Education Act (ESEA) and Title IX requirements and takes its responsibilities under the law seriously.
“ The safety and well-being of our students is our highest priority. CTECS remains fully committed to complying with all ESEA and Title IX requirements and takes its responsibilities under the law seriously. We will cooperate with the U.S. Department of Education’s review to ensure our reporting and compliance practices are consistent with federal law and reflect the steps we take to ensure the safety of the students in our care ,” the school system said in a statement.
Attorney John Manly, who represents victims of child sexual assault in schools, released the following statement:
“Parents entrust public schools with the important duty of keeping their kids safe. Schools throughout the nation, including Connecticut Technical Education and Career System, have failed. Many have allowed known molesters to remain in the classroom and prey on children. A recent study published by Harvard Education Press indicates that every year up to 10% of all K-12 public-school students are subject to a wide range of sexual misconduct by public school employees, conduct which includes rape. That is a national catastrophe and a hidden scandal which must be exposed, and I am grateful that the Department of Education and the Trump Administration are taking concrete action to stop it. Congress should join in a bipartisan effort to hold public hearings and hold our nation’s school administrators and school board members accountable.”
